name: Macau
operatingHours: Macau Light Rapid Transit runs ~6:30 AM–~11:15 PM daily, every ~5–10 min. Lines: Taipa Line (Barra on the peninsula, under the sea to Taipa, Cotai and the airport), the short Seac Pai Van spur, and the Hengqin Line from Lotus across to Hengqin (mainland China, immigration required). Most of the old peninsula is not on the LRT; buses, taxis and free casino shuttles fill the gaps.
fareInfo: LRT single fares MOP 6–10 by distance (2026); tap a Macau Pass stored-value card or pay by mobile QR at the gates, or buy a single-journey token. City buses charge a flat ~MOP 6 (cheaper with Macau Pass). Big resorts run free shuttle buses between Cotai, the peninsula, the ferry terminals and the border gates.

sights.name: Ruins of St. Paul's
sights.note: The carved stone façade of a 17th-century Jesuit church, all that survived an 1835 fire, reached by a broad staircase from a lane of almond-cookie shops; a small crypt museum sits behind it.
sights.hours: Façade open 24 hours; crypt museum 9:00 AM–6:00 PM (closed Tue afternoon); free

sights.name: Largo do Senado (Senado Square)
sights.note: The wave-patterned Portuguese cobblestone square at the heart of the UNESCO-listed historic centre, ringed by pastel colonial buildings and the start of the walk up to St. Paul's.

sights.name: Monte Fort & Macao Museum
sights.note: A 17th-century Jesuit fortress beside the Ruins of St. Paul's with cannons and city views; the Macao Museum inside its walls tells the city's East-meets-West story.
sights.hours: Fort 7:00 AM–7:00 PM; museum 10:00 AM–6:00 PM, closed Mon

sights.name: St. Dominic's Church
sights.note: A yellow-and-white baroque church just off Senado Square, founded by Dominicans in 1587, with a small sacred-art museum in its bell tower.

sights.name: A-Ma Temple (Ma Kok Miu)
sights.note: Macau's oldest temple, built into the hillside in honour of the sea goddess Mazu and believed to have given the city its name; Barra LRT station is across the square.

sights.name: Mandarin's House
sights.note: A sprawling restored courtyard mansion from the 1860s, once home of the reformist thinker Zheng Guanying, mixing Chinese and Western design.

sights.name: Chapel of Our Lady of Penha
sights.note: A hilltop chapel on Penha Hill with one of the best free viewpoints over the Inner Harbour, the bridges and Taipa.

sights.name: Macau Tower
sights.note: A 338 m tower with an indoor observation deck and glass floor at 223 m; thrill-seekers can do the outer SkyWalk or one of the world's highest bungy jumps.
sights.hours: Observation deck ~10:00 AM–9:00 PM (weekends from ~9:00 AM)

sights.name: Guia Fortress
sights.note: Hilltop fort with China's oldest Western-style lighthouse and a small chapel with restored frescoes; reach it on the short Guia cable car from Flora Garden.
sights.hours: Fort 9:00 AM–6:00 PM; chapel 10:00 AM–5:30 PM; free

sights.name: Lou Lim Ieoc Garden
sights.note: A tranquil Suzhou-style garden of rockeries, lotus ponds and zigzag bridges built by a wealthy merchant family, popular with locals for morning tai chi.

sights.name: Macau Grand Prix Museum
sights.note: Racing cars, motorcycles and simulators celebrating the street circuit that has hosted the Macau Grand Prix since 1954.

sights.name: Taipa Village
sights.note: Old Taipa's narrow lanes of colonial houses, temples and snack shops, centred on Rua do Cunha for pork-chop buns, egg tarts and almond cookies.
sights.hours: Lanes open 24 hours; shops ~10:00 AM–10:00 PM

sights.name: The Venetian Macao
sights.note: The giant Cotai resort with indoor canals, gondola rides under a painted sky and a vast shopping arcade beside one of the world's biggest casino floors (casino 21+).
sights.hours: Resort open 24 hours; shops ~10:00 AM–11:00 PM

sights.name: Eiffel Tower at The Parisian Macao
sights.note: A half-scale Eiffel Tower replica at The Parisian resort with an observation deck on the 37th level overlooking the Cotai Strip; lit up nightly.

sights.name: Wynn Palace Performance Lake & SkyCab
sights.note: A free fountain show set to music on the lake in front of Wynn Palace, best seen from the free SkyCab gondolas that glide around it.

sights.name: Macau Giant Panda Pavilion
sights.note: A hillside enclosure in Seac Pai Van Park on Coloane where giant pandas, including Macau-born twins, can be watched indoors and out; pandas are most active in the morning.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–1:00 PM and 2:00–5:00 PM, closed Mon

sights.name: Coloane Village
sights.note: A sleepy former fishing village with the cream-and-white Chapel of St. Francis Xavier, seafront cafés and the original Lord Stow's egg-tart bakery.

airports.name: Macau International Airport
airports.transitNote: On Taipa; Airport station on the LRT Taipa Line (shown on this map) is by the terminal: ~10 min to the Cotai resorts, ~25 min to Barra on the peninsula. Bus AP1 runs to the ferry terminal and Border Gate; taxis ~MOP 60–100 to the peninsula. Taipa Ferry Terminal (Hong Kong ferries) is one LRT stop away.
airports.hours: LRT: first train ~6:30 AM, last ~11:15 PM. Late arrivals: bus, taxi or a hotel shuttle.
